newsitem.title: USA: FDA deputy Friedman to temporarily lead agency.
newsitem.headline: FDA deputy Friedman to temporarily lead agency.

text.p: A senior Food and Drug Administration official, Dr. Michael Friedman, will temporarily lead the agency while the search continues for a permanent successor to Dr. David Kessler, officials said.
A spokesman for Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala said Friedman will serve as "lead deputy commissioner." He was not formally named acting or interim director.

Kessler has announced he is leaving the agency, and will probably depart in late February. Friedman, one of three top deputies to Kessler, already has some day-to-day operational responsibilities at FDA.

Friedman has often been cited as a possible successor to Kessler but many Washington observers believe Shalala will go outside the FDA for a new commissioner who has not been embroiled in controversies in the past few years.
